title: Prior auth tracker for a 6-provider orthopedic practice
one_liner: Tracks every prior authorization from submission to decision, flags denials with a reason, and routes appeals before the payer deadline.

practice.name: Riverside Orthopedic Associates
practice.type: Orthopedic practice, outpatient imaging and procedures
practice.size: 6 providers, 2 locations, ~40 prior auth requests per week

persona.name: Dana Whitfield
persona.day_in_the_life: Dana starts at 7:30am with 12 open auth requests across 4 payers. She checks each payer's portal separately, writes status updates into a shared spreadsheet, and calls two payers whose auths are overdue past the 5-business-day SLA. By 9am she's found a denial from Meridian Health Partners for case #4471, decided 3 business days ago but nobody saw it — the appeal window is 5 business days from the decision, so only 2 business days remain and no one has started the appeal.

problem.current_workflow: Auth status lives in a shared spreadsheet, updated manually from four different payer portals with no reminders. Denials sit unread until someone happens to check the portal.
pain_points: No single view of auth status across payers
Denials are discovered late, after days have already passed on the appeal clock
Appeal deadlines are tracked from memory, not from a system
No record of which denial reasons recur, so the practice can't fix root causes
problem.cost_of_pain: Dana estimates 6-8 hours per week re-checking portals manually, and the practice loses an estimated $14,000 per quarter in missed-deadline denials that could have been appealed.

story.before: 7:30am: Dana opens the spreadsheet and four payer portals in separate tabs. She manually copies status for 12 open cases. At 8:52am she happens to notice, while checking an unrelated case, that case #4471 (Meridian Health Partners, lumbar MRI for patient J. Alvarez) was decided 3 business days ago: denied for 'missing clinical documentation.' The appeal window is 5 business days from the decision date — only 2 business days remain, and no one has started the appeal.
story.after: 7:30am: Dana opens the tracker. The dashboard already shows case #4471 flagged red in Denials, 'Denied — missing documentation,' with 2 business days left on the clock and the missing document already identified. Dana attaches the missing clinical note, moves the case into the Appeals queue herself, reviews the drafted appeal summary, and submits it in two clicks. Nothing moved on its own — she drove every step. She moves to the next flagged case; all 12 open cases are visible in one list with days-to-SLA shown for each.

edge_case.scenario: Case #4471 (Meridian Health Partners, lumbar spine MRI, patient J. Alvarez) is denied with reason code 'missing clinical documentation' — the referring physician's progress note wasn't attached to the original submission.
edge_case.how_handled: The case appears in the Denials screen flagged red with the specific missing item named and a live countdown (computed from decision_date and appeal_deadline, never a written-in number) to the appeal deadline. Dana attaches the missing document and moves the case into the Appeals queue herself; nothing moves automatically.
edge_case.label: missing clinical documentation

human_checkpoint.what_staff_does: Dana reviews the identified missing document and the drafted appeal summary, attaches the correct file, and clicks 'Submit appeal' — nothing is sent to the payer without her explicit action.

metrics.label: Average days to decision

metrics.label: Denial rate
metrics.computed_from: Count of cases where status equals denied, divided by count of cases where status is approved or denied, last 30 days by decision_date

metrics.label: Appeals won
metrics.computed_from: Count of denied cases where appeal_status equals won

entities.name: Prior auth cases
entities.realism_notes: Roughly 60% submitted/pending, 25% approved, 15% denied. Denials spread across 4 plain-language reasons (missing documentation, not medically necessary per policy, incomplete clinical info, duplicate request). Payers are all fictional: Meridian Health Partners, Palmetto Health Plan, Lakeshore Mutual, Crestview Benefits. Among denied cases, appeal_status is distributed roughly 40% none, 30% submitted, 20% won, 10% lost. Case #4471 is the edge case: Meridian Health Partners, lumbar MRI, patient J. Alvarez, submitted_date = 10 business days before decision_date, decision_date = 3 business days ago (denied, 'missing clinical documentation'), appeal_deadline = decision_date + 5 business days (so 2 business days remain as of today), appeal_status = none until the tour's Appeals step moves it to submitted.

entities.name: Case notes
entities.realism_notes: 2-3 notes per case on average across 85 cases, timestamps relative to each case's submitted_date, written in plain operational language ('Called the payer, on hold 20 min, no update').

tour.title: Meet Dana
tour.body: Dana manages prior auth for a 6-provider orthopedic practice. Here's her morning before and after this tool.

tour.title: Every case, one view
tour.body: All open and recent prior auth cases across every payer, with days remaining on each SLA.

tour.title: Full case history
tour.body: Every submission, call, and document for a case, in one timeline.

tour.title: A denial, caught immediately
tour.body: This case was denied for a missing clinical note. The system flagged it the moment the payer responded, not days later.

tour.title: The clock is visible
tour.body: A live countdown to the appeal deadline. No more guessing from memory.

tour.title: Dana still decides
tour.body: Nothing goes back to the payer until Dana reviews it and clicks submit herself.

tour.title: The numbers that matter
tour.body: Open cases, average decision time, denial rate, and appeals won — all computed from real case data.

tour.title: How this would be built
tour.body: This concept maps to the practice's existing tools: Epic for records, Availity and payer portals for submission, with human approval before every payer-facing action.

compliance_notes: Patient data would be stored encrypted at rest and in transit
All payer-facing submissions require explicit staff approval before sending
Access is role-restricted to authorized billing staff, with full audit logging
Any AI-assisted document review operates under a signed BAA; no PHI is sent to a model without one
Only the minimum necessary case data is shared with each integrated system

design.rationale: A deep green grounded in clinical calm, with a muted amber accent used only as a fill (never as text color) for alerts and deadlines, pairs a serif for headings (credibility, unhurried) with a clean humanist sans for data-dense tables.
